label: Extension selects skills whose 0-2 expected rubric index is >= 2*threshold (default 0.375), caps at 12, skips filtering below 8 skills, and fails closed after 8000 ms; config errors force fail-closed.

Advisor passes a recommendation on confidence >= threshold AND uncertainty <= threshold; confidence is a floored ramp (0.82 floors, 0.72 derived pin, 0.95 ceiling) and the hook bench pins 0.8/0.35; resolver defaults inferred, not read.

Both scores are rubric indices, not probabilities; the advisor's 0.82 floors collapse evidence differences like the extension's expectation does, so uncertainty and a floored-count diagnostic are the better separating signals (inference).

REJECT a hosted per-skill score as a fusion replacement: default policy measured precision 0.39 / recall 1.00 with ~10 of 30 kept, 254-5704 ms picker time versus a 3000 ms hook timeout, and prompt egress on every call.

ADAPT: run a decision-model score off the hook path as a shadow tie-break over ambiguity-cluster members only, logged to the existing shadow sink via cli-jev, never changing the brief until a per-model threshold is calibrated.

REJECT porting the 0.375 default: the extension's own sweep shows best floors from 1.0 to 1.75 per model (jev F1 0.40 at default vs 0.88 at 1.75); any model lane needs a per-model, per-version threshold.

ADAPT the benchmark method: add a no-skill negative-control abstain metric and a required/acceptable label split to advisor routing benchmarks; the advisor already has Brier/ECE reliability gates the extension lacks; whether golden prompts hold expected-null rows is UNKNOWN.
REJECT the 8-skill inventory floor: it protects a filtered native skills section, while the advisor adds a push brief and removes nothing (inference).
